pr_body:
There is a small race condition in the tenant directory cache.

1. If ReportFailure is called, the tenant dir rebuilds the cache by listing the available pods.
2. There is a watch attempting to push events to the cache. If an event was generated before the most recent list, the watch event can roll back cache state.

This race is okay in production because when the sql proxy tries to dial the stale pod, the dial will fail and the proxy will refresh the list again.

This change adjusts the test to work like production. If the list is stale, ReportFailure is retried to refresh the list of pods.

Fixes: #86077
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/107299)

comments:
I think this is a race condition within the tenantdir cache. It is a known interaction between the tenantdir's watch and list RPCs.

The kernel of the race is this:
1. If ReportFailure is called, the tenant dir rebuilds the cache by listing the available pods.
2. There is a watch attempting to push events to the cache. If an event was generated before the most recent list, the watch event can roll back cache state.

Here are the relevant logs from the test failure:
```
I220813 05:42:33.353771 3564 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go:236 ⋮ [-] 91  fetched IP addresses: [‹tenant_id:50 addr:"127.0.0.1:46875" state:RUNNING stateTimestamp:<seconds:1660369353 nanos:353693615 >›]
I220813 05:42:33.353830 3564 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go:197 ⋮ [-] 92  resumed tenant {50}
I220813 05:42:33.353864 3564 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go:104 ⋮ [-] 93  refreshing tenant {50} pods
I220813 05:42:33.354087 3564 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go:236 ⋮ [-] 94  fetched IP addresses: [‹tenant_id:50 addr:"127.0.0.1:46875" state:RUNNING stateTimestamp:<seconds:1660369353 nanos:354011693 >›]
W220813 05:42:33.355188 4589 sql/sqlliveness/slinstance/slinstance.go:242 ⋮ [tenant=50,nsql1] 97  exiting heartbeat loop
I220813 05:42:33.361736 3564 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go:104 ⋮ [-] 102  refreshing tenant {50} pods
I220813 05:42:33.362528 4632 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/directory_cache.go:456 ⋮ [-] 103  added IP address ‹127.0.0.1:46875› with load 0.000 for tenant 50
I220813 05:42:33.362580 4632 ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/directory_cache.go:463 ⋮ [-] 104  deleted IP address ‹127.0.0.1:46875› for tenant 50
```

Note the log line "fetched IP" indicates the pod was inserted by a list. The log line "added IP" indicates the pod was inserted by the watch.

This is what occurred in this test run:
1. The sql server is started. The creation watch event is delayed.
2. The test calls dir.ReportFailure, this refreshes the cache and the cache includes the test server.
3. The test shuts down the sql server.
4. The test calls dir.ReportFailure, this refreshes the cache. Since the sql server is shut down, the List returns no pods and the cache is cleared.
5. The watch event for the server creation is finally delivered. This inserts the sql server into the cache.
6. The test asserts the cache is empty, but in reality the cache the stale pod entry.

We could fix the test by waiting for the initial event instead of calling ReportFailure to refresh the cache. The better fix would be to rework the tenantdir cache entirely. IMO The ListPods calls are of dubious value. I think we would be better off removing the list calls and relying entirely on watches.

cc: @jaylim-crl

The race is described in a TODO
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/5d7e232ddf11d505f45815df7ada7d08e6ce26e1/pkg/ccl/sqlproxyccl/tenant/entry.go#L219-L223

review_comments: I also recalled that if we wanted to fully mimic production, we should update WatchPods to stream a list of pods that the server knows about when it first gets called.
That is a case we should test, but it's a bit orthogonal to the test directory server in general. The test directory server always starts empty, so there are no watch events to propagate.

> The test directory server always starts empty

There are some tests that simulate a crash of the tenant directory server, or the Watch API closing early.
